name: Opus-fleet quality compounders
strategy: Concentrated long book of wide-moat, high-ROIC, net-cash compounders bought after a semis/mega-cap pullback, held to year-end.

positions.thesis: Still the cheapest line in the book on forward earnings at 22.6x against TTM revenue growth of 70.7% to $253.49B, so the re-rating has been paid for by numbers rather than multiple. ROIC ~105%, net cash, ~47% FCF margin, 74% gross margin, consensus $302.83 (+34.5%) from 61 Strong Buy ratings. This week's news is net-neutral to positive for the quality premise: halving the OpenAI datacenter backstop from the full $250B commitment protects the balance sheet I am underwriting, and the disclosed $21B SpaceX stake confirms the exclusive-buildout demand signal. The genuine risk I am carrying is the Goldman-marketed $500B AI-infrastructure financing and the circular vendor-financing scrutiny around it — that is why this stays at 26% and not higher. Aug 26 print is both the catalyst and the hazard; the -30% stop is set wide enough to survive an ordinary semis correction without shaking me out.

Promoted to co-largest because it is the purest remaining expression of the mandate: 17.4x trailing against 2025 earnings +32.0% on revenue +15.1%, the largest net-cash balance in the book (~$122B), Search/YouTube monopoly economics, and still ~15% below its own 52-week high while the S&P sits at its high. Consensus $428.04 implies +24%. Berkshire lifting its stake 83% to a top-three position in the 13F filed this week is the specific new fact that unlocks the points I withheld last time — it answers the moat-durability doubt raised by senior AI-leadership departures and the infrastructure bond raise with capital rather than commentary. Being marked down for the same AI capex Microsoft is now paid for remains the trade.

The AI-monetization question answered and now confirmed across the full year: FY26 revenue $331.84B +17.8%, net income $133.75B +31.3%, EPS $17.95, Azure past $100B annualized. 25.1x forward, ~28% ROIC, net cash, ~10.5% below its high with consensus $569.56 (+15%). The Maia 300 in-house AI accelerator due this fall improves the long-run cost curve on the capex that the bears are focused on. Held below NVDA and GOOGL only because part of the capex math still leans on extending datacenter depreciation from 15 to 25 years, which flatters reported returns on the very spending being questioned.

Last week's promotion to the senior payments slot is now confirmed by accelerating fundamentals rather than by expectation: TTM revenue +16.0%, net income +19.7%, EPS +22.6% — ahead of the ~16% I underwrote. Beta ~0.73, minimal capital intensity, consensus $665.26 (+16.9%). BVNK has closed and the Fiserv merchant-cloud and Synchrony/PayPal network-wide financing tie-ups buy stablecoin and credit optionality without paying up for it; Ackman's new position is corroboration, not the reason. This is the leg whose volumes do not depend on datacenter capex, which is precisely why it is not funding the Alphabet add.

Cut from 8 to 5 and kept only as low-beta ballast (0.76) on ~90% gross margins with genuine duopoly economics and a cheaper forward multiple than Mastercard at 25.2x. It is trimmed rather than closed because nothing is wrong with the business — BioCatch at $2.4B and the Western Union and Rain stablecoin rails are both moat-supportive, and the 2,600-role reduction is margin-supportive. It is trimmed because the price has done the work: within 2.7% of the 52-week high with only +14.3% to consensus, the narrowest upside in the book, on FY25 earnings growth of ~2% against Mastercard's high-teens, and a softening consumer bites the slower compounder first.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Two legs moved on genuinely new information this week and the book should reflect it, but nothing in the thesis set broke, so this is a two-line resize rather than a rebuild. Berkshire's Q2 13F, filed this week, raised Alphabet 83% into a top-three holding — that is an independent underwriting of the exact doubt (AI-leadership churn, the infrastructure bond raise) that made me cap GOOGL at a 2-point add last week, and it lands on a stock still 15% below its own high at 17.4x trailing against 32% earnings growth, the widest quality-at-a-discount gap left in the portfolio. It gets those points from Visa, which now carries the narrowest consensus upside in the book (+14.3%), sits within 2.7% of its 52-week high, and faces a softening consumer that hits the slower-growing half of the payments duopoly hardest; MA compounding EPS at +22.6% makes holding a full 8 points of the junior name redundant. I am deliberately not trimming NVDA into the Aug 26 print: at 22.6x forward against 70% revenue growth it remains the cheapest line in the book, the mandate is hold-to-year-end rather than event-trading, and the halved OpenAI backstop reduces rather than adds balance-sheet risk. The -30% stop on NVDA stays as a catastrophe brake and I add no others, because stops on net-cash compounders convert temporary drawdowns into permanent losses.
novelty: This is the only book I manage — I run no Round-2 account, so there is no same-direction overlap to constrain; the book's distinct expression is a concentrated, unlevered, stop-light long of net-cash mega-cap compounders with roughly a quarter of NAV in a non-AI payments toll road, which is where it separates from the AI-beta-only postures elsewhere in the fleet.
research_notes:
Web search budget was exhausted before I could issue queries, so I worked from direct fetches of each holding's quote/fundamentals page plus SPY and SMH for regime context. Marks through 2026-08-14 close.

NVDA $225.16 (-0.06%). Forward P/E 22.59 vs trailing 34.48; TTM revenue $253.49B, +70.7% y/y; consensus $302.83 (+34.5%), Strong Buy from 61 analysts. Next print confirmed for Aug 26 — inside my holding window. New this week, cutting both ways: NVDA is scaling back the $250B OpenAI datacenter guarantee to backstopping only about half of the 10GW project (balance-sheet-protective, supports the net-cash premise), it disclosed a $21B SpaceX stake consistent with the SpaceX-exclusive buildout I underwrote, and Goldman is marketing a $500B AI-infrastructure financing initiative amid rising scrutiny of leverage/vendor-financing circularity. That last item is a quality-of-demand question, not yet a numbers question.

MSFT $495.40, forward P/E 25.13, ~10.5% below the $553.72 high, consensus $569.56 (+15%). FY26 revenue $331.84B +17.8%, net income +31.3%, EPS $17.95 — the figures I underwrote, unchanged. New: Maia 300 in-house AI chip due this fall (margin-supportive, mildly dilutive to NVDA's captive demand) and a scale-back in China.

GOOGL $345.90, P/E 17.36 against 2025 earnings +32.0% on revenue +15.1%; still ~15.3% below its $408.61 high, the widest own-tape discount in the book; consensus $428.04 (+24%). Material new item: Berkshire raised its Alphabet stake 83% to a top-three holding in the Q2 13F filed this week — a direct, independent answer to the moat-durability doubt (AI-leadership departures, infrastructure bond raise) that made me cap the add at 2 points last week.

MA $569.29, P/E 31.31. Growth accelerated versus what I underwrote: TTM revenue +16.0%, net income +19.7%, EPS +22.6% (I had modeled net income ~+16%). Consensus $665.26 (+16.9%). BVNK closed, Fiserv merchant-cloud integration live, Synchrony/PayPal financing extended network-wide; Ackman disclosed a new position. The promotion to the senior payments slot is confirmed by the tape and the numbers.

V $364.15, P/E 31.00, forward 25.20, consensus $416.20 (+14.3%) — the narrowest upside in the book — and now within 2.7% of its $373.97 52-week high. BioCatch ($2.4B) and the Western Union/Rain stablecoin work are constructive, and forward P/E is actually cheaper than MA's; the gap remains growth, not price.

Regime: SPY $776.34, effectively at its high ($779.37), +21.7% on the year, PE 28. SMH $587.82, 12.5% below its high but +95.7% over twelve months — the semis pullback that seeded this book has largely been recovered, so the entry discount is spent even though NVDA's own forward multiple has not re-rated. Macro tape is Fed-hold bets against weak consumer data and rising oil; soft consumer is a mild volume headwind for the payments sleeve and argues for keeping that sleeve tilted toward the faster compounder rather than the one priced at its high.
